fields.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses.
fields.note: The source-of-income bar, the Section 8 example, the list of protected classes, the advertising ban, and the 180-day and two-year filing periods are all in the document. The document does not mention the $10,000 first-offense fine. It also does not mention the landlord's remaining grounds to refuse (insufficient income, oversized family, zoning, poor credit).

fields.quoted_span:
You may file a complaint with us for free within 180 days
of the date of the alleged violation.
fields.note: The source-of-income protection, the 180-day DCR window and the two-year Superior Court window are supported. The 'fines up to $10,000 for a first offense' part does not appear anywhere in this document.
The field is empty and the document states no effective date for the provision.

fields.quoted_span:
The Division on Civil Rights enforces the New Jersey
Law Against Discrimination.
fields.note: The present-tense statement of enforcement is consistent with the law being in force. The document does not say so in terms.

fields.quoted_span:
The rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family
dwelling, the other occupancy unit of which is occupied
by the owner as his/her residence at the time of such
rentals;
fields.note: The general scope, the owner-occupied two-family exemption, the room-rental exemption, the religious-organization preference and the older-persons exemption (for familial status) are all in the document. The single-sex residence (YMCA) exemption is not in this document; it comes from D067.
The document never cites N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g). It cites only N.J.S.A. 10:5-5mm, for the definition of housing for older persons. It does name the Law Against Discrimination (LAD).
